headline_marked: OpenAI in talks to give US a [[5% stake]] for public AI benefit
headline: OpenAI in talks to give US a 5% stake for public AI benefit
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman discusses 5% stake with Trump administration
details: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is in active talks with the Trump administration about the US potentially acquiring a 5 percent stake in the leading AI firm. Insiders say Altman has argued that giving the public a financial stake in the company is the best way to share the upside of AI.

The talks are in early stages, and Altman has discussed the idea with Trump officials such as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, as well as Senator Bernie Sanders. Sanders has proposed a larger sovereign public wealth fund, which would require a one-time 50 percent tax on AI firms' stock.

OpenAI's proposal aims to give Americans more control over AI and benefit from its growth. The company has suggested creating a sovereign wealth fund similar to the Alaska Permanent Fund, which invests oil wealth into stocks and pays dividends to the state government and residents.

The discussions come as AI firms face growing public skepticism, with 70 percent of Americans opposing AI data centers in their area and half more concerned than excited about AI. OpenAI and other firms may be willing to give a stake to the public if it helps gain acceptance and trust.
